_note: Dilemmas that can fire in either chapter. Keep these free of chapter-specific vocabulary — a dilemma in here must read correctly whether the player is the Mayor or the Chair. Anything that assumes the Nexus, the Apocrypha or hidden authority belongs in chapter2.json.

dilemmas.title: Eleven hours dark
dilemmas.prompt: The ladder did what you told it to. The workshop kept its power and the clinic went dark for eleven hours, and a woman who would probably have lived did not. The ladder was set eight months ago, by you, on a quiet afternoon, and it was the right decision at the time.

options.label: Reorder the ladder
options.detail: Medical above industry, permanently. Accept the output cost.

options.label: Stand by it
options.detail: Say plainly that the order is correct and that this is what it costs.
options._note: Legitimacy rises while trust falls. Owning an unpopular decision reads as strength even to people it hurt — the clearest case for legitimacy being a separate axis from trust.

options.label: Fund a battery bank
options.detail: Solve it with hardware instead of a policy. It will take a month.

dilemmas.title: The grove, or ninety people
dilemmas.prompt: Cultivation has run the numbers unasked. Three slots of grove would feed ninety people. The trees were planted before anyone on the Board was born, by a committee that left a note about what they were for, and the note is in the archive if you want to read it.

options.label: Clear it
options._note: Ends paper production for the rest of the run once existing wood runs out — which means it ends the Accord's supply line. The consequence nobody reads on the way past.

options.label: Take one slot
options.detail: Thin it. Keep enough for paper and ceremony, and grow food in the rest.
